source.title: Beyond Black Boxes: Enhancing Interpretability of Transformers Trained on Neural Data
source.authors: L. Freeman; Philip Shamash; Vinam Arora; C. Barry; T. Branco; Eva L. Dyer

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different method from toy-model superposition research: it trains an SAE on POYO+ neural-data latents and measures feature selectivity, reconstruction, and effects of feature-targeted ablations.
record.gate_note: The study tests SAE feature interpretability and selectivity, but does not test whether sparse features compete for limited dimensions, whether they form overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, or whether polysemanticity reflects capacity pressure. Its neural-data transformer is not an LLM. Reported decoding-performance preservation and biological coefficient comparisons do not establish superposition geometry.
record.test_reason: The study applies a TopK-SAE as an interpretability tool to POYO+, a transformer trained on mouse calcium-imaging data. It reports how well its own pipeline works: decoding is preserved, SAE latents are more selective than baseline latents, and ablations of SAE latents have targeted effects. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry or capacity competition (V1, V2). It does not test non-capacity origins of polysemanticity (V3) or feature spread in LLMs (V4), since the model is not an LLM. It does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable across runs or canonical (V5), nor feature dimensionality (V6). The reader's V5 link rests on selectivity and ablation results, which do not address what V5 asserts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that integrating a TopK-SAE into POYO+ preserves decoding performance with a modest drop. They find it yields more selective, interpretable latents that mirror known biology (VIP directional selectivity), and that it enables targeted, feature-specific ablations. They acknowledge residual entanglement: SST ablation did not fully abolish SST decoding because some latents mix SST and VIP information.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a TopK-SAE on latents from a neural-data transformer and evaluates selectivity, decoding, reconstruction, and ablations; it does not use toy networks or test superposition as a function of feature sparsity or importance.
record.method_sensitivity: The SAE uses TopK sparsity; the paper reports a sweep from TopK 5 to 30 and selects TopK = 20 for the reported best reconstruction variant. Interpretability analyses are restricted to VISp and drifting gratings.

fits_no_version.finding: In a transformer trained on neural data, TopK-SAE latents are more stimulus-selective than baseline latents (median fraction of bins 0.4 vs 0.9). They align with single Cre-lines, and ablating them has targeted effects, though SST ablation leaves residual decoding because some latents mix SST/VIP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs recover more selective, causally targetable units than raw latents in non-language transformers (e.g., neural-data decoders).

fits_no_version.finding: Inserting the SAE costs about 5% decoding accuracy (baseline ≈45%, SAE >40%) and about 0.05 R² on running speed (baseline ≈0.57). Reconstruction R² is 0.885 at TopK=20.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE insertion into a neural-data transformer incurs a small downstream performance cost.

record.problems: Evidence is restricted to VISp and drifting-gratings analyses. The orientation-ablation effect is described without numerical accuracies. The paper itself reports residual entanglement and incomplete SST decoding after ablation. It does not establish feature identity stability or a complete feature inventory.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the tested claim version were omitted.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, no feature-count versus dimension test, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
All of it: no test of capacity competition or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
All of it: the model is a neural-data transformer, not an LLM, and feature spread across neurons is not measured.
Completeness, stability of feature identity across SAE runs, and canonicality are not tested. Only selectivity and ablation effects of one SAE configuration are reported.

record.verdict_notes: I reclassified this study from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. The SAE is used as a tool, and the reported results are the tool's performance compared with baseline latents, which the rules exclude as rows bearing on versions. The VIP vs SST coefficient consistency across 8 checkpoints (Fig. 5) concerns aggregate coefficient patterns, not identity stability of individual features, so it does not test V5 stability either. Note that Appendix 5.3 describes an L1 sparsity loss term while Section 2.2 says no sparsity penalty is used, an internal inconsistency.

versions.untested_parts: No test of feature-count versus dimensionality, feature sparsity or importance effects, overlap geometry, or a sparsity-dependent transition.
No test of whether features compete for capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
No test of polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
The study analyzes a transformer trained on mouse neural data, not LLMs; it does not test feature spread in LLMs.

It measures selectivity, reconstruction, and some causal effects of SAE latents, but does not establish a complete feature inventory or stable, canonical correspondence of individual features across independently trained SAEs.
The study analyzes one-dimensional SAE latent units but does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: POYO+
rows.size_stated: POYO+ latents d = 64; SAE latents D = 192
rows.stage_stated: POYO+ was previously trained; the SAE was trained on POYO+ latents
rows.operation_detail: Compared the fraction of stimulus bins above a high-confidence activation threshold for SAE and baseline latents.
rows.measure: Median fraction of orientation–frequency bins exceeding the threshold
rows.note: The text describes the SAE latents as significantly more selective; it gives no p-value.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method (SAE latents) with the baseline latents on a selectivity metric. It measures tool performance, not completeness, stability or canonicality of the dictionary features, so it bears on no version.

rows.subject: POYO+
rows.size_stated: Input latent dimension d = 64; SAE expansion factor = 3
rows.stage_stated: POYO+ was previously trained; the SAE was trained on POYO+ latents
rows.operation_detail: Measured reconstruction of baseline latents by the SAE at the selected TopK setting.
rows.measure: R² between baseline latents and SAE reconstructions
rows.baseline: Baseline latents as reconstruction reference; baseline R² not stated
rows.note: Reconstruction is substantial but not complete; the text identifies TopK = 20 as the best variant.
rows.check: This is a reconstruction R² at a selected TopK (selection value from a sweep). It describes the SAE's fidelity, not whether its features are the model's canonical units. The 'partial' state has no version to be judged against.

rows.subject: POYO+
rows.size_stated: Baseline latent dimension d = 64; SAE latent dimension d = 192
rows.stage_stated: POYO+ was previously trained; the SAE was trained on POYO+ latents
rows.operation_detail: Compared how individual dimensions in baseline and SAE representations aligned with genetic Cre-line labels.
rows.measure: Qualitative selectivity of individual dimensions for Cre-line labels
rows.baseline: Baseline dimensions typically mix multiple Cre-lines
rows.value: SAE dimensions respond selectively to individual Cre-lines, with examples for SST- and VIP-expressing neurons
rows.note: This is evidence of selective label alignment, not proof of a complete or canonical feature inventory.
rows.check: This is qualitative UMAP-based alignment of SAE latents with Cre-line labels, framed as method performance. It does not test completeness, stability or canonicality.

rows.subject: POYO+
rows.stage_stated: POYO+ was previously trained; the SAE was trained on POYO+ latents
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed SAE latents selected for tuning to the 0° orientation and measured orientation-decoding accuracy.
rows.measure: Orientation-specific decoding accuracy after targeted latent ablation
rows.baseline: Accuracy before ablation; exact value not stated
rows.value: A substantial drop for the 0° stimulus, with minimal impact on other orientations
rows.note: The reported direction and selectivity of the effect are stated, but numerical accuracies are not.
rows.check: This is a targeted ablation validating the method's selectivity. No numbers are given, and it does not bear on any version as stated.

rows.subject: POYO+
rows.stage_stated: POYO+ was previously trained; the SAE was trained on POYO+ latents
rows.operation_detail: Ablated SAE latents associated with SST interneurons and measured Cre-line decoding.
rows.measure: SST and VIP Cre-line decoding accuracy
rows.baseline: SST accuracy 0.73; baseline VIP accuracy not stated
rows.uncertainty: p < 0.05 for the SST decrease; VIP effect described as not significant
rows.note: The authors state that SST decoding was not fully abolished and that some latents encode mixed SST and VIP information.
rows.check: This is an SST-latent ablation (0.73 to 0.56) with residual mixed latents. It reflects incomplete disentanglement by the tool, not a test of V5's claims that features are complete, stable and canonical.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE latent selectivity and targeted feature ablations in POYO+ on VISp drifting-gratings data
reader_labels.reason: SAE latents had a lower median fraction of active stimulus bins than baseline latents, aligned selectively with Cre-line labels, and targeted ablations produced feature-specific effects (r1, r3, r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SAE reconstruction and SST-associated ablation in POYO+
reader_labels.reason: Reconstruction was not complete (R² = 0.885), and SST ablation only partly reduced decoding; the authors report residual mixed information in some latents (r2, r5).
